description: Build the API layer (Refit interface, Contracts records, PagesClient wrapper, request-context handler with the commented multi-tenant placeholder) and the API test suite: eight scenarios covering page-list shape, the page_size-vs-returned-count rule, pagination headers asserted as present-and-positive rather than equal to a live count, the per_page boundary-value outlines at 0/1/100/101, a slug lookup and a 404. Depends on FEAT-001 for the solution, configuration layer and utilities. Independent of FEAT-003.
steps: Create the Contracts records under d:\git\QAAutomation\src\QAAutomation.Api\Contracts: RenderedText.cs (Rendered); WordPressPageResponse.cs (Id, Slug, Link, Title as a RenderedText); WordPressErrorResponse.cs (Code, Message); PageListResponse.cs (HttpStatusCode StatusCode, List<WordPressPageResponse> Pages, string TotalCountHeader, string TotalPagesHeader, WordPressErrorResponse Error); PageLookupResponse.cs (HttpStatusCode StatusCode, WordPressPageResponse Page, int MatchCount, WordPressErrorResponse Error). The last two wrapper records exist so step definitions never touch HttpResponseHeaders or a Refit type directly, which step-definitions.md forbids.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\src\QAAutomation.Api\Clients\IWordPressApi.cs - the Refit interface. [Get("/pages")] Task<IApiResponse<List<WordPressPageResponse>>> GetPagesAsync([AliasAs("per_page")] int perPage, [AliasAs("_fields")] string fields, CancellationToken cancellationToken); a second [Get("/pages")] method taking [AliasAs("slug")] string slug plus the fields and token; and [Get("/pages/{pageId}")] Task<IApiResponse<WordPressPageResponse>> GetPageAsync(int pageId, [AliasAs("_fields")] string fields, CancellationToken cancellationToken). Always IApiResponse<T>, never bare T, so 400 and 404 are inspected rather than thrown.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\src\QAAutomation.Api\Clients\PagesClient.cs - the wrapper that steps inject. Methods ListPagesAsync(int perPage, CancellationToken), FindPagesBySlugAsync(string slug, CancellationToken) and GetPageByIdAsync(int pageId, CancellationToken), each returning the Contracts wrapper record. Read header values through Core's HeaderValueReader. Read the error body by casting response.Error to ApiException and deserialising .Content into WordPressErrorResponse with System.Text.Json, guarding for a null or non-ApiException error. Hold the field selection in a named const string FieldSelection = "id,slug,title,link". No assertions, no test data generation, no literal base URL - the base URL comes from ApiOptions. When picking the single matching page out of a slug search, use an explicit foreach with a break into a named variable, never LINQ.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\src\QAAutomation.Api\Clients\RequestContextHandler.cs - a DelegatingHandler that adds the correlation-id header from ScenarioCorrelation, carrying a clearly commented placeholder block for the KEYinfinity multi-tenant request-context pattern described in api-automation.md section 3. The comment must state that on KEYinfinity the tenant is a REQUIRED EXPLICIT parameter with no ambient default and no static current-tenant, that this handler is template-only scaffolding to be replaced by that explicit parameter, and that WordPress has no tenancy so there is nothing to pass or assert here yet. Never log the header values.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\src\QAAutomation.Api\ApiRegistration.cs with AddApiClients(IServiceCollection, ApiOptions): register RequestContextHandler transient, then services.AddRefitGeneratedClient<IWordPressApi>().ConfigureHttpClient(client => { client.BaseAddress = ...; client.Timeout = ...; }).AddHttpMessageHandler<RequestContextHandler>(), then PagesClient scoped. It MUST be AddRefitGeneratedClient<T>() - AddRefitClient<T>() fails at run time demanding the separate Refit.Reflection package. The ConfigureHttpClient lambda is permitted under code-style.md exception 2 because the API accepts nothing else.

Create the test project wiring at d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.Api: reqnroll.json containing { "language": { "feature": "en-GB" } }; AssemblyInfo.cs with [assembly: Parallelizable(ParallelScope.Fixtures)] and [assembly: LevelOfParallelism(2)] - read-only GETs, but kept low because the target is a production site; PageApiContext.cs with int RequestedPageSize, PageListResponse ListResponse and PageLookupResponse LookupResponse; and ApiScenarioDependencies.cs with a static [ScenarioDependencies] factory calling TestConfigurationLoader.Load(), AddTestConfiguration, AddApiClients and registering PageApiContext and ScenarioCorrelation scoped. Register NO driver and create NO hooks class - the API suite must not be able to launch a browser.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.Api\Features\PageListing.feature with feature-level tags @api @regression @marketing and a coverage-note comment stating the site is live so no exact count is ever asserted. Scenarios, in order: (@smoke) 'Requesting the page list returns published pages' - When a page list is requested with a page size of 2 / Then the page list request succeeds / And every returned page carries an identifier, a slug, a title and a link. 'The page list never returns more pages than the requested page size' - same When / Then the page list request succeeds / And no more pages are returned than were requested. 'The page list reports how many pages exist in total' - same When / Then the page list request succeeds / And the pagination headers report positive whole numbers. Then two Scenario Outlines, preceded by a comment explaining the accepted and rejected partitions are separate tables because their Then differs, so the expected outcome lives in the Then rather than in a column that would be constant for every row: 'A page size inside the documented range is accepted' with 'Examples: accepted page size boundaries (boundary value analysis)' and rows 1 and 100; 'A page size outside the documented range is rejected' with 'Examples: rejected page size boundaries (boundary value analysis)' and rows 0 and 101.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.Api\Features\PageLookup.feature with feature-level tags @api @regression @marketing and a comment noting the slug is live third-party content configurable through Site:KnownPageSlug. Scenarios: (@smoke) 'Looking up a published page by its slug returns one fully formed page' - When the page with the slug "technical" is requested / Then the page lookup succeeds / And exactly one page is returned / And the returned page carries an identifier, a slug, a title and a link. 'Looking up a page identifier that does not exist is refused' - When the page with an identifier that does not exist is requested / Then the page lookup reports that the page was not found.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.Api\Steps\PageListingSteps.cs and Steps\PageLookupSteps.cs as async Task bindings with constructor-injected PagesClient, PageApiContext and SiteOptions. Keep every body to one or two client calls then an assertion. Use AwesomeAssertions only, with a because reason on every non-obvious assertion, and group the two pagination-header checks inside one AssertionScope so the scenario keeps a single assertion concern.

In the pagination-header step, read X-WP-Total and X-WP-TotalPages through Core's PositiveIntegerParser and assert only that each header is PRESENT and parses to a POSITIVE INTEGER. Add a comment stating plainly why: X-WP-Total changes the moment Landmark publishes a page, so hard-asserting 18 or any other live count would make the suite go red for no product reason - this is the most important lesson the template teaches. Likewise the page-size step asserts pages.Count <= RequestedPageSize, never an equality.

In the rejected-page-size step assert the exact status code 400 and that Error.Code equals a named const InvalidParameterErrorCode = "rest_invalid_param". In the missing-identifier step read Site:MissingPageId from SiteOptions rather than hard-coding 999999 in the step, and assert the exact status code 404. Iterate returned pages with explicit foreach loops and named locals to check shape - no LINQ anywhere.
acceptance_criteria: dotnet build d:\git\QAAutomation\QAAutomation.sln reports 0 Warning(s) and 0 Error(s), in particular no Refit RF006 diagnostic (which would mean a method cannot generate inline and the generated-client registration would fail at run time).
dotnet test d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.Api passes all 8 scenarios with 0 failed and 0 skipped.
dotnet test d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.Api --filter "TestCategory=smoke" runs and passes exactly 2 scenarios, proving tag-to-category filtering.
No step definition or feature file contains a hard-asserted live content count, a raw URL, an HTTP header name, a status-code literal outside a named constant, or any LINQ.
The API test project registers no IWebDriver and contains no [Binding] hooks class.
findings:
SURPRISE 1 - COLD-START FLAKE THAT FEAT-003 AND FEAT-004 WILL ALSO HIT. The first `dotnet test` run after a fresh build failed 1 of 9 with `SetUp : Reqnroll.BoDi.ObjectContainerException : Concurrent object resolution timeout (potential circular dependency)` thrown from `DependencyInjectionPlugin.CustomizeFeatureDependenciesEventHandler` during `PageLookupFeature.TestInitializeAsync`. Cause: with `[assembly: Parallelizable(ParallelScope.Fixtures)]` both feature files start within milliseconds, the first `[ScenarioDependencies]` factory call takes just over a second on a cold JIT (configuration + IHttpClientFactory + the Refit generated client), and Reqnroll's BoDi lets the second thread wait only 1 second. Reproduced deterministically with `dotnet build --no-incremental` followed immediately by `dotnet test --no-build`; it never reproduces on a warm second run, which is what makes it expensive. FIX: `tests\QAAutomation.Tests.Api\ContainerStartup.cs` - an `internal static` class with a `[ModuleInitializer]` method setting `Reqnroll.BoDi.ObjectContainer.DefaultConcurrentObjectResolutionTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60)`, with a long plain-English comment. It is NOT a hook: a `[BeforeTestRun]` hook class is itself built by the container, so it runs too late to change how the container waits; `[ModuleInitializer]` runs at assembly load, which is the only point early enough. COPY THIS FILE (namespace changed) INTO Tests.UI AND Tests.E2E - they use the same parallelism and their factories are heavier still, because they also build the driver stack. Verified: two consecutive cold `--no-incremental` build + test cycles both reported `Failed: 0, Passed: 9`.

SURPRISE 2 - `IApiResponse.StatusCode` is `HttpStatusCode?`, not `HttpStatusCode`, in Refit 16.3.0. Assigning it straight to a non-nullable property is `error CS0266`. Handled in `PagesClient.ReadStatusCode(IApiResponse)`, a private helper that throws `InvalidOperationException` with a plain message naming `Api:BaseUrl` when the value is null, because a missing status code means the request never reached a server (bad host, timeout, no network) and a fake status code would make a step report a confusing mismatch instead. The wrapper records therefore expose a non-nullable `HttpStatusCode`, which is what keeps `Should().Be(HttpStatusCode.OK)` readable in the steps.

SURPRISE 3 - SCENARIO COUNT IS 9, NOT 8. The acceptance criterion and context.json both say 8 API scenarios, but `PageListing.feature` has 3 plain scenarios plus two Scenario Outlines of 2 rows each (7 test cases) and `PageLookup.feature` has 2, so the suite is 9 test cases from 7 scenario definitions. The planned scenario set was built exactly as specified in FEAT-002 step 7 and step 8 - nothing was added - so 8 was an arithmetic slip in the plan. `dotnet test` reports `Failed: 0, Passed: 9, Skipped: 0`. The whole-solution expectation in context.json should therefore be 18, not 17, once FEAT-003 (8 UI) and FEAT-004 (1 E2E) land.

SURPRISE 4 - `reqnroll.json` is copied to the output directory automatically. The Reqnroll build targets pick it up with no `<None CopyToOutputDirectory>` item in the .csproj; verified present in `bin\Debug\net10.0\` next to `appsettings.json`. Do NOT add an explicit None item for it in Tests.UI or Tests.E2E - that risks a duplicate-item error for no benefit.

URL COMPOSITION, SETTLED - Refit concatenates the configured base path with the method path rather than letting HttpClient re-resolve it, so a base URL of `https://www.landmarksystems.co.uk/wp-json/wp/v2` plus `[Get("/pages")]` reaches `.../wp-json/wp/v2/pages` correctly (proven by 9 live passes). `ApiRegistration.BuildBaseAddress` trims a trailing slash from the configured value so the settings file can be written either way without producing a doubled slash, which would 404 and look like a product fault.

API SURFACE FEAT-004 (E2E) WILL CALL:
- `QAAutomation.Api.ApiRegistration.AddApiClients(this IServiceCollection, ApiOptions)` - registers `RequestContextHandler` transient, the Refit client via `AddRefitGeneratedClient<IWordPressApi>()` with `ConfigureHttpClient` (base address + timeout) and `AddHttpMessageHandler<RequestContextHandler>()`, and `PagesClient` scoped. It REQUIRES `ScenarioCorrelation` to be registered by the caller (the handler takes it as a constructor dependency); `AddTestConfiguration` does not register it, so the E2E factory must call `services.AddScoped<ScenarioCorrelation>()` exactly as `ApiScenarioDependencies` does, or the first request throws.
- `QAAutomation.Api.Clients.PagesClient` (scoped): `ListPagesAsync(int perPage, CancellationToken)` -> `PageListResponse`; `FindPagesBySlugAsync(string slug, CancellationToken)` -> `PageLookupResponse` (throws `ArgumentException` on a blank slug); `GetPageByIdAsync(int pageId, CancellationToken)` -> `PageLookupResponse` (throws `ArgumentException` on a non-positive id). Field selection is fixed at the const `"id,slug,title,link"`.
- `PageLookupResponse { HttpStatusCode StatusCode; WordPressPageResponse Page; int MatchCount; WordPressErrorResponse Error; }`. `PageListResponse { HttpStatusCode StatusCode; List<WordPressPageResponse> Pages; string TotalCountHeader; string TotalPagesHeader; WordPressErrorResponse Error; }`. `Pages` is an EMPTY list, never null, on a refusal, so a step can count it without a null check.
- `WordPressPageResponse { int Id; string Slug; string Link; RenderedText Title; }` with `RenderedText { string Rendered; }`. For the E2E title rule use `Page.Title.Rendered` as the case-insensitive SUBSTRING of the browser title, and `Page.Link` as the URL to navigate to - guard that link with `UrlHostChecker.HasSameHost(SiteOptions.BaseUrl, link)` first, because it is a value from a response.
- Contracts carry explicit `[JsonPropertyName]` attributes rather than relying on a naming policy, so no serialiser options are configured anywhere.
- Step phrases already taken by the API suite, and therefore unavailable to a new binding without an ambiguity failure: "a page list is requested with a page size of {int}", "the page list request succeeds", "every returned page carries an identifier, a slug, a title and a link", "no more pages are returned than were requested", "the pagination headers report positive whole numbers", "the page list request is rejected as an invalid parameter", "the page with the slug {string} is requested", "the page with an identifier that does not exist is requested", "the page lookup succeeds", "exactly one page is returned", "the returned page carries an identifier, a slug, a title and a link", "the page lookup reports that the page was not found". These live in a DIFFERENT ASSEMBLY from Tests.E2E, so they are not inherited - the E2E suite must define its own bindings, and it may safely reuse the wording.

STEERING COMPLIANCE NOTES: no LINQ anywhere (recursive scan for `System.Linq`, `.Where(`, `.Select(`, `FirstOrDefault`, `.Any(`, `.All(` over both projects returns only a code comment in `PagesClient` explaining why a `foreach`+`break` is used instead of `FirstOrDefault`). The only lambda in the API layer is `ConfigureHttpClient`, which is exception 2. Status codes are `HttpStatusCode` enum members, never literals. Header names (`X-WP-Total`, `X-WP-TotalPages`) and the error code (`rest_invalid_param`) are named consts - the header names in `PagesClient`, the error code in `PageListingSteps`. The API test project registers no `IWebDriver`, never calls `AddBrowserSupport`, and has no `[Binding]` hooks class.
